name: Proton Mail
description: Proton Mail is an encrypted email service with messages, conversations, folders, labels, contacts, desktop Bridge interoperability, and custom-domain SMTP submission.
agentUseSummary: Proton Mail cannot currently be connected because mailbox interoperability requires a paid, continuously running same-device Bridge that decrypts mail locally and exposes local IMAP/SMTP credentials. Proton's other supported automation credential is a send-only custom-domain SMTP token; neither is Relay-owned delegated OAuth or compatible with Railway execution without a new product/runtime decision.

blocked.label: Connect through delegated OAuth
blocked.description: Proton does not publish a stable third-party Mail API with developer registration, delegated scopes, callback, refresh, and revocation lifecycle.

blocked.label: Use Proton Mail Bridge
blocked.description: Bridge is a paid local process that authenticates to Proton, decrypts mail on the same device, and exposes session-specific local IMAP/SMTP credentials; it cannot serve Railway-hosted tools.

blocked.label: Use an SMTP submission token
blocked.description: A manually generated token is bound to one paid custom-domain address and permits only sending, requiring a separate high-risk write product.

blocked.label: Use Proton's private client API
blocked.description: Open-source first-party Bridge/API libraries and their SRP, token, key, and private endpoint machinery are not a supported third-party provider contract.

blocked.label: Access Proton Mail data
blocked.description: Addresses, messages, conversations, drafts, attachments, folders, labels, contacts, searches, moves, deletes, sends, exports, raw protocols, and every read or write remain unavailable.

approvalProfiles.label: Unavailable
approvalProfiles.description: No agent action can be enabled until Relay approves a local-only Bridge or send-only SMTP product, or Proton publishes delegated Mail OAuth.

runtimeSupport.description: A same-device Bridge cannot be mounted through Railway as OpenClaw tools, and the SMTP-only product is not approved.
A same-device Bridge cannot be mounted through Railway as Hermes tools, and the SMTP-only product is not approved.

providerSetup.blocker: Proton mailbox reads require a paid same-device Bridge and local decrypted-mail boundary, while SMTP submission is a user-owned send-only token; no public delegated Mail OAuth/API contract exists.
providerSetup.nextAction: Do not request Proton Account, Bridge, or SMTP credentials and do not show Connect. Reconsider after an explicit local-runtime or send-only product decision, or after Proton supplies a public partner Mail API with delegated authorization and encryption responsibilities.

evidence.supports: Proton documents Bridge as the required local component that decrypts encrypted mail and exposes IMAP/SMTP to same-device desktop clients.
Proton does not provide ordinary remote IMAP/POP mailbox access; Bridge supplies separate local credentials rather than the Proton Account password.
Proton SMTP submission uses manually created, address-bound, revocable tokens for sending from paid custom-domain addresses and provides no mailbox reads.
Proton's open-source API library is used by its own Go clients and tools; source availability does not establish a stable supported third-party Mail API contract.
